resolutionEvidence: The SAME $((10#$x)) base-10-forcing guard is now applied at all 3 arithmetic sites: skills/profitable-article-writer/run.sh:119 (_modeb_ratio_n, before -eq 0), run.sh:144 (_modeb_next_wake_count, before increment), and run.sh:166-167 (the actual modulo deciding effective_mode=B -- the exact previously-unguarded site named by this finding). Traced by hand: $wake_n/$ratio_n are already leading-zero-free by construction when they reach lines 166-167, so this guard is a provably-safe, non-spurious belt-and-suspenders re-check, not a new inconsistency.
description: REQ-25 states 'a div/mod-by-zero or parse error SHALL be caught' (an explicit, deliberate error-handling requirement) for the ratio-consultation logic. Tracing the actual code in run.sh shows this requirement is only PARTIALLY implemented, and inconsistently between the two call sites of the same hazard: at line 105 ('if [ "$n" -eq 0 ] 2>/dev/null'), the author explicitly redirects stderr to /dev/null around a numeric comparison -- circumstantial evidence the author is already aware bash's numeric evaluator can raise an error here (the ONLY realistic error source for a regex-validated all-digit string reaching '-eq' is the leading-zero/octal case described in FIND-001) -- yet the identical hazard at the OTHER call site that actually performs the mod computation, line 133 ('if [ $((wake_n % ratio_n)) -eq 0 ]'), has NO such suppression and no try/catch-equivalent guard at all. This is an inconsistent, incomplete implementation of the 'SHALL be caught' requirement: one occurrence of the exact same class of error is defensively muted, the other -- the one that actually decides whether effective_mode becomes 'B' -- is not, meaning the correctness of the fail-closed behavior for this input class currently depends on incidental bash control-flow semantics (a failed arithmetic expansion happening to make the enclosing '[ ]' test evaluate false) rather than on code that was deliberately written and tested to handle it, which is what REQ-25's 'SHALL be caught' text requires.

evidence.snippet:
if [ "$n" -eq 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then   # error suppressed here
  return 1
fi
...
if [ $((wake_n % ratio_n)) -eq 0 ]; then   # NOT suppressed / guarded here
  effective_mode="B"
fi

recommendation: Same fix as FIND-001 (reject leading-zero digit strings at the regex/validation stage in _modeb_ratio_n, before either call site can ever receive an unsafe operand) closes this gap at its source; alternatively, wrap the line-133 modulo with the same explicit error-suppression-and-fail-closed pattern already used at line 105, and add a test proving the specific behavior (not merely that it 'happens to work').
